question: Which kinds of updated components on Ubuntu normally force a reboot because they can't easily be swapped out in a running system, unlike editors or CLI tools?
answer: The kernel and the core libc, since they affect everything and can't be easily replaced in a running system.
support: the kernel or the core libc that affect everything will require a reboot

question: Which group of classic Gang of Four design patterns is said to exist mainly as workarounds for deficiencies in programming languages, so a more expressive language wouldn't need them?
answer: A majority of the GoF patterns fall into this category of language-deficiency workarounds.
support: Some design patterns are workarounds for deficiencies in programming languages.

question: In GNU Readline, which two history search functions ship with no default key binding and search using the text between the start of the line and the cursor?
answer: history-search-forward and history-search-backward (can be bound to M-n and M-p in place of the non-incremental searches).
support: history-search-forward history-search-backward Search forward/backward through the history for the string of characters between the start of the current line and the point.

question: In Oracle, how can I build a view that pairs every descendant location with the third-level building it sits under in a self-referencing parent/location table?
answer: Use CONNECT_BY_ROOT location, with START WITH limited to rows at LEVEL 3 (found via a CONNECT BY PRIOR location=parent subquery) and CONNECT BY PRIOR l.location = l.parent.
support: SELECT connect_by_root location "Building", location "SubLocation" FROM some_table l START WITH l.Location IN

question: Our CI server's Python builds are slow because packages are re-downloaded every time. Rather than keeping persistent virtualenvs around, what is the suggested fix for a network throughput bottleneck?
answer: Use an artifact repository to cache packages locally, keeping each build idempotent instead of reusing virtualenvs.
support: If you find you are blocked by network throughput, consider using an artifact repository to cache packages locally.

question: What is a real-world production use of EIGRP offset-lists that one network engineer describes at their organization?
answer: Forcing traffic onto a particular backup WAN link when the primary link has problems but hasn't actually gone down.
support: force traffic to take a particular backup WAN link when the primary is having issues that don't actually take it down

question: Why does nmap OS fingerprinting work poorly on Android phones and other handhelds, and what little does it have to go on?
answer: They often listen on no ports, so nmap lacks TCP handshake responses and only has closed-port responses and ICMP echo replies.
support: Without an open port all nmap has to work on is the response to closed ports and ICMP echo replies.

question: If DBAN isn't an option, what dd command from a root shell, writing about a megabyte at a time, can scramble a running Linux server's disk so it's unbootable?
answer: dd if=/dev/urandom of=/dev/sda bs=1000k, after shutting down as many services as possible (especially the windowing system).
support: dd if=/dev/urandom of=/dev/sda bs=1000k

question: A startup with zero users keeps worrying about scaling. What problem does one answer say they actually have instead of a scalability problem?
answer: A number-of-users problem; solving scalability first means solving a problem they don't have yet.
support: you don't have a scalability problem; you have a number-of-users problem

question: In terminal vim, how can I bind a function key so it pops up completion of the gvim-style menu entries without typing the :emenu command each time?
answer: :set wildcharm=<C-Z> then :map <F4> :emenu <C-Z> (after loading menus with :source $VIMRUNTIME/menu.vim and :set wildmenu).
support: :set wildcharm=<C-Z> And make a binding that automatically invokes :emenu completion for you: :map <F4> :emenu <C-Z>

question: With an assemblies table and a parts table joined on AID, how do I return every part in any assembly that contains the part named 'Part B', including Part B's siblings?
answer: LEFT JOIN parts p USING (AID) with WHERE p.AID IN (SELECT AID FROM parts WHERE P_NAME='Part B').
support: WHERE p.AID IN ( SELECT AID FROM parts WHERE P_NAME='Part B' );

question: When trying to win over a low-acceptance organization to DevOps tooling, what kind of evidence suits software developers versus executive stakeholders?
answer: Developers want to see it in action via proofs of concept with measurable outcomes; executives may accept case studies and presentations.
support: software developers ... want to see it in action, so POC's with measurable outcomes are preferred

question: PC1 at 192.168.1.2 pings PC2 at 192.168.2.2, which has no default gateway. What source address does the router put on the packet it forwards to PC2 so the reply can work?
answer: 192.168.2.1, the router's own address on segment 2 (NAT rewrites the source), so PC2 replies locally to the router.
support: Router sends src=192.168.2.1 dst=192.168.2.2 to PC2ether on seg2

question: Can I discover which DKIM selector a domain uses to sign its mail without first receiving a message from that sender?
answer: No; you need a mail, extract the selector from its DKIM-Signature header, then query DNS for it. Guessing common selectors proves nothing either way.
support: There is no way to detect if DKIM is implemented by the sender without getting a mail from the sender, extracting the selector from the DKIM-Signature header

question: I set up a certificate on my EC2 web server but HTTPS isn't reachable from outside. Which security group rule should I check, and what quick command tests it?
answer: Allow TCP port 443 in the instance's Security Group; test with telnet yourhost.com 443 and see if you connect.
support: make sure that port 443 is allowed over TCP ... telnet yourhost.com 443

question: If a client's requirements are fully known and won't change, what benefit does a short-iteration agile process still give beyond refining vague requirements?
answer: Early feedback about the real effort and costs, which even a detailed waterfall approach can still get wrong.
support: It will also give you early feedback about the real effort and costs

question: In a POSIX shell without arrays, how do I strip every occurrence of one particular argument, such as -inf, out of the positional parameters?
answer: for arg do shift; [ "$arg" = "-inf" ] && continue; set -- "$@" "$arg"; done
support: for arg do shift [ "$arg" = "-inf" ] && continue set -- "$@" "$arg" done

question: In PostgreSQL, how does the efficiency of the GIN and GiST indexes used on jsonb columns compare with a plain b-tree index on an ordinary column?
answer: GiST and GIN are generally much less efficient; a b-tree on a normal column will almost always be much, much faster.
support: GiST and GIN indexes like those used on jsonb are generally much less efficient than a plain b-tree index.

question: To decouple CI tooling data from servers with an immutable architecture, which tools are suggested for static analysis, artifact storage, base images and deployment?
answer: SonarQube static analysis in CI, artifacts pushed to Nexus, Packer base images, deployment via Terraform and Ansible, Jenkins 2.0 pipeline as code.
support: CI with static analysis(Sonarqube, because free!), pushing version artefacts to Nexus. Base Image using Packer.

question: How many security contexts can a Cisco ASA active/standby failover pair run if each unit has only the base license?
answer: Up to four, because each unit's two-context base license is shared across the failover pair.
support: If you create an active/standby failover pair up to four contexts can be created as the licensing is shared between the physical devices.
